title: Publish the Cohort Community Code of Conduct, Anti-Bullying, and Moderation Playbook, by Fri 4 Dec
description:
As technical bootcamps and virtual academies scale to hundreds of concurrent learners, toxic communication, harassment in direct messages, and academic dishonesty undermine cohort retention. Academy operators currently lack standardized moderation workflows, role-based disciplinary procedures, and safety escalation ladders inside Zedu workspaces. This playbook delivers a comprehensive trust, safety, and community moderation system tailored for cohort operators.

Work under this goal:
- Formulate the Zedu community code of conduct and student pledge template covering channel etiquette, direct message boundaries, and intellectual property standards.
- Write the step-by-step community moderator operations protocol: identifying infractions, utilizing channel muting/removal controls, and managing private disciplinary review channels.
- Design the anonymous harassment and academic grievance reporting thread workflow utilizing Zedu's private thread drawer and DM protocols.
- Draft the student appeal and restorative resolution template pack stored and shared via Zedu File Management.

Done when: A complete trust and safety operations guide is delivered with copy-ready community guidelines, moderator triage checklists, disciplinary escalation matrices, and channel permission configurations verified against live zedu.chat controls.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Build the moderation playbook on the controls Zedu has today, and list the missing ones as product gaps
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A moderation protocol only works if every step uses a real control. In the production code (Cybertron-HNG/zedu-fe, cybertron-integration, 22 Oct 2026) moderators have: 'Delete message' in the message menu (ChannelMessage/more.tsx line 257), 'Remove from channel' in channel details (channel-details-tabs-content.tsx line 412), 'Posting restricted' per channel (channel management), 'Archive channel', and 'Mute participants' in Buzz calls. I found no 'Report message' or 'Block user' control anywhere in the app, and the pricing page lists AI Moderation as Enterprise-only. So learners can't report harassment in-app today. Plan: 1) write the code of conduct and student pledge; 2) write the moderator protocol as an escalation ladder using only those five controls, plus a private admin channel for disciplinary review; 3) design the harassment and grievance route outside the app for now (a monitored form or email with response times), and give the product team a short gap list: in-app report, user block, and DM moderation. Tasks: code of conduct and pledge (content), moderator protocol and escalation ladder (content), grievance route and product gap list (research).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Give disputed moderation decisions a documented appeal and correction route
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The accepted approach covers current controls and first-response escalation, and the pending integrity idea defines collaboration rules. This complementary approach covers what happens when a learner disputes a decision or a moderator makes an error: one appeal template, acknowledgement wording, an impartial review checklist, a correction/restoration template and an outcome notice. Establish proposed roles and conflict-of-interest handoff without inventing named staff, response-time promises or app features. Distinguish a process recommendation from Zedu capabilities; a verified, team-approved contact route is a launch dependency, and no anonymous/private reporting guarantee is made. Deliver one coherent appeal-and-correction appendix that attaches to the existing playbook, with three fictional tabletop cases (mistaken deletion, disputed copying allegation, report involving a moderator). Acceptance: each case identifies evidence needed, the independent reviewer role, what the affected person can challenge, the privacy boundary and a reversible corrective action; unresolved product limitations are explicit. The team must confirm age/guardian handling, record retention and urgent escalation before use. Measure whether reviewers can trace a decision and correction without exposing learner records; no invented real cases, appeal outcomes or compliance assurances. No live investigation, disciplinary decision, user restriction, contact or publication.

A documented appeal and correction route is the missing half of moderation: it covers the decision a learner disputes or a moderator gets wrong.
A code of conduct without an appeal path leaves enforcement one-sided. An appeal route with a named reviewer is the missing half of the anti-bullying playbook.
First-response controls do not cover the case where a moderator is wrong. An appeal and correction route makes the playbook complete without duplicating the accepted approach.

This adds an important appeal-and-correction step beyond initial moderation: learners can challenge mistakes and a reviewer can document a reversible correction. It avoids inventing named staff or response promises, uses fictional cases, and makes team confirmation of contact, age and retention rules a prerequisite.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Write the academic-integrity section separately: what counts as collaboration vs copying in coding cohorts, with examples
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Harassment and academic dishonesty need different handling, and coding cohorts mostly argue about the second. Approach: define allowed help (explaining an approach, pair debugging, sharing docs) vs not allowed (posting full solutions to graded tasks, submitting another learner's code), with 8 concrete examples. Set where solutions may be shared (a staff-controlled channel after the deadline), and a proportionate response ladder from a private reminder to an escalation to the programme lead. Done: the integrity section, the examples, the response ladder and the pinned short version.
